summary.headline: Deep Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR278.92 crores, EBITDA margin 43.6%, net profit INR89.14 crores (+44.5%), order book INR3,047 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR278.92 crores and EBITDA rose 38.7% to INR131.8 crores at a 43.6% margin, with net profit up 44.5% to INR89.14 crores. Management said the company has held EBITDA margins in a 43-45% range and attributed the quarter to operational efficiencies. Growth drivers cited were offshore (Dolphin), the ONGC production enhancement contract (PEC), and Dubai subsidiaries, with the standalone business guided to grow only 18-20% in FY27. Management reiterated FY28 PAT ambition of about INR500 crores and said there are no further Kandla legacy write-offs this year.

financial_highlights.metric: Dubai subsidiaries plus Indian subsidiary other revenue

financial_highlights.value: 75-80% historically; Q1 said to be on similar lines

segments.name: Gas processing
segments.commentary: Charter Hire model for gas processing plants; operating from 3 fields (2 ONGC, 1 Cairn). Management says capacity can be increased as opportunities arise.

segments.name: Gas compression and dehydration
segments.commentary: Management says Deep has executed about 85% of outsourced gas compression work in India and owns more than 80 compressor units. Standalone revenue has been flat at around INR175 crores for 5 quarters.

segments.name: Onshore drilling and workover rigs
segments.commentary: Fleet of 20 rigs (14 workover, 6 drilling of 1,000 HP) at 100% utilisation. Management is evaluating 2,000-3,000 HP rigs with bids expected in the next few months.

segments.name: Production enhancement (ONGC contract)
segments.commentary: INR1,402 crore, 15-year contract. Incremental production delayed 5-6 months by a well incident at Mori-5; incremental output expected from around September-October 2026. FY28 revenue guided at more than INR150 crores.

segments.name: Offshore (Dolphin Offshore)
segments.commentary: Two assets fully deployed: DP2 barge Prabha (3-year contract, expected to contribute more than INR150 crores a year) and AHTS V, which has no long-term contract. Further tugs and barges planned over 3-5 years, capex only after firm orders.

guidance_outlook: FY28 PAT target of almost INR500 crores; management said FY27 PAT expected to be about INR350 crores.
Standalone revenue growth of 18-20% in FY27 and consolidated growth above 25%; standalone revenue expected to improve from Q2 as 4-5 gas compression and processing contracts start.
Blended EBITDA expected to improve in FY28 as offshore and PEC contribute at higher margins; offshore margins expected to exceed onshore.
Kandla hydrocarbon fluids unit expected to contribute from later in FY27, adding about 1.5% to EBITDA margin with INR10-15 crores of capex and no debt.
Capex of around INR250-300 crores in FY27 for higher-capacity rigs, contingent on firm orders; PEC capex of about INR150 crores by March 2027.
About INR800 crores of order book expected to be executed in FY27; more than 60% of the order book to be executed over 2-2.5 years.
capex_capacity: PEC incremental production expected from around September-October 2026; new wells to contribute in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; PEC capex of about INR150 crores by March 2027.
Higher-capacity (2,000-3,000 HP) drilling rig bids expected in the next few months; funding via debt and internal accruals once awarded.
Offshore fleet expansion planned over 3-5 years (tugs, barges, 1-2 support vessels), capex only after firm contracts.
Kandla facility revival requires INR10-15 crores, no debt planned.
Management does not foresee an equity raise; net debt-free position.
demand_pricing: Order intake has been roughly equal to execution over the last 4-5 quarters; management expects a similar run rate and some larger contracts.
Contracts are largely fixed-price, tender-driven L1 bidding; the company bears no exploration success risk.
PEC block is under a free-price mechanism; spot gas prices quoted at USD 8-15/MMBtu, with management not expecting a fall below USD 8.
Onshore rig market estimated at 215-220 rigs (about 120-125 outsourced); outsourced share rising.
Bidding pipeline about INR700-800 crores; none of the three strategic priorities (PEC tender, DSV/PSV, higher-HP rig) yet in the pipeline.
Inquiries from Vedanta, ONGC and Oil India increased, which management attributed to both pre-existing demand and the current geopolitical situation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kandla facility a margin lever and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says reviving Kandla to make a chemical used in drilling and integrated project management improves EBITDA margin by about 1.5%, with INR10-15 crores of capex and no debt; no further write-offs expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 PAT of INR450-500 crores achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is gunning for almost INR500 crores PAT in FY28 and expects about INR350 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much does the Mori PEC well and incremental production matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mori was beyond expectations with high-pressure gas, but Mori-5 is not operating after the incident; other wells around it may be explored. Incremental output expected from around September-October 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for standalone business given flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects standalone growth of 18-20% in FY27 as new gas compression and processing contracts start from late Q1/Q2, with consolidated growth above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Offshore pipeline and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Two assets (Prabha DP2 barge and AHTS V) fully deployed; no current bid pipeline, though several tenders are being evaluated; offshore contracts would be fixed-price charter hire.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Dolphin contribution sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Prabha barge contract of 3 years expected to contribute more than INR150 crores a year; further growth in FY28 expected with fleet additions.

risks_watch: Mori-5 well incident delayed PEC incremental production by 5-6 months; restart timing (Sept-Oct 2026) and new well contribution (Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28) to monitor.
Standalone revenue flat at around INR175 crores for 5 quarters; 18-20% FY27 growth depends on new contract starts from Q2.
Offshore growth depends on winning firm tenders; AHTS V not on long-term contract and contributing little.
Green hydrogen tender outcome pending; geothermal and hydrogen remain at evaluation stage with partners.
Order book conversion: about INR800 crores expected to execute in FY27 of INR3,047 crores.
Clarity needed on the new PEC tenders (Gamij, Geleki) that an analyst said carry higher minimum fixed fees; management declined to comment until awarded.
key_quotes: We believe it should. With the momentum currently going on, it won't surprise us if we can do that much.
So, currently, we have 1 -- we have 2 assets and which are completely deployed. So, utilization of the current assets is complete.
So, it wouldn't be fair for us to comment about what our strategies would be and what kind of revenue visibility would it be because we have not yet been awarded.
Capital expenditure is strictly committed only upon securing firm deployment contracts.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on demand, citing policy tailwinds, a 40% revenue rise and a stated FY28 PAT ambition of about INR500 crores. It was noticeably cautious on specifics: it declined to comment on the new PEC tenders until awarded, would not give capex or offshore pipeline numbers without firm orders, and hedged on the Mori-5 well incident and on the timing of new rig bids.

adds.what: PEC incremental production from ONGC contract (INR1,402 cr, 15-year) after Mori-5 well delay
Higher-capacity 2,000-3,000 HP drilling rigs (bids expected in next few months)
Offshore fleet expansion (tugs, barges, 1-2 support vessels) over 3-5 years, capex only after firm contracts

growth.why: Standalone FY27 revenue guided at 18-20% and consolidated above 25%, backed by INR3,047 cr order book (about INR800 cr to execute in FY27), 4-5 gas compression/processing contracts starting from Q2, and PEC incremental output from Sept-Oct 2026 after a 5-6 month Mori-5 delay; rig and offshore expansion remain contingent on firm orders.
